title: The edge table
description:
The closed edge vocabulary, with the cardinality a validator enforces and the traversal policy expansion reads. Every field that names another node and must resolve is an edge here; a relationship stated only in prose is not an edge, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs.

**This table is the only home the vocabulary has.** It was written as a third copy — the specification stated it in prose, `EDGE_KINDS` in the materializer held a hand transcription, and nothing compared them. The specification has since been removed, so what was a transcription is now the statement, and the copy in `EDGE_KINDS` is the one that has to agree with this file rather than the reverse. See `x-agreement`.

`out` is edges leaving one node; `in_max` is edges arriving at one target, which is how at-most-one-lifecycle-per-definition becomes a check. `null` is unbounded.

x-agreement.state: The eleven edges both hold agree on every compared column. The two that differ are the two breaks this tree applies and the shipped side has not: `governed_by` is here only under `x-removed`, and `steps[].ko` there is `steps[].node` here.
x-agreement.open: Nothing performs this comparison. It was held by a test module removed with the rest of `tests/`, and the state recorded above was established by hand. A table whose agreement is asserted rather than checked drifts the same way the three copies did.

boundary.note: Every node but a subdomain and a context declares exactly one. Membership is derived from this field; a scope never enumerates what it holds.

depends_on.note: The only content edge that may cross a bounded context, and the target must then be an interface. It is also the edge a rule declares to name what it constrains.

lifecycle.subject.note: `in_max: 1` is what makes 'no two lifecycles claim one subject' a cardinality check rather than a special case.

transitions[].emits.note: The target's ddd is `domain-event` or `integration-event`. A transition emitting an api or a command names something a state change does not raise.

rejections[].error.note: The target is a definition whose ddd is domain-error.

steps[].node.note: Spelled `steps[].ko` in domain-object/1. The rename is the vocabulary change this tree applies and the shipped contract has not.

steps[].compensated_by.note: What undoes a step. Absent on a step that needs no compensation, and on every process that is not a saga.

context_relationships[].with.note: Traversed only when expansion crosses a context.

payload.note: Required of every ddd but `api`, or a gap naming it. `in_max` is unbounded: one definition may shape several interfaces, and a published language exists to be shared.

upstream.note: Declared by the consumed side and required of it. `in_max` is unbounded because that is the point — the count of edges arriving at a published interface is the answer to who depends on it, and it is derived rather than declared.

x-removed.governed_by: Carried by `domain-object/1` as an edge to a decision record, `adr.NNNN`. A decision record is a graph node and never a knowledge object, and this framework holds no decision-record node — so every target is one the base cannot hold, and the materializer exempted `adr.` targets from resolution rather than reporting them. **It does not come back, and this is a decision rather than an omission.** A domain graph records what the business decided, not the deliberation that reached it; tracing a boundary to the discussion behind it is version control's work. Removing it is a breaking change to the frontmatter contract.
x-removed.superseded_by: Named a node and was never an edge. The field is gone; the name must appear in no vocabulary derived from this table.

x-open: `crosses_context` is set on three edges here — boundary, subdomain, context_relationships[].with — plus depends_on, whose exemption is conditional on the target being an interface. `src/claude/schemas/knowledge-graph.json` says the flag is 'True only for the three edges whose purpose is to leave or to name a partition' and `src/claude/bin/materialize.py` sets it on none. The three the shipped schema means are not named anywhere, so this column is a reading and not a transcription.

`crosses_context: true` on `boundary` says a node may belong to a scope in another context. Nothing states that this is wanted, and `src/claude/bin/check_knowledge.py` now reports it as a disagreement between a node's identifier and its parent — so the column and the check contradict each other. The check is the one that matches every other statement in this tree; this column is what is owed a correction.
The `in` column's minimum is not modelled. Nothing requires a node to be referenced; whether an unreferenced node is a defect is the orphan rule, not a cardinality bound.

`depends_on` and `steps[].node` carry `target: null`, so a process step may name a subdomain and a rule may depend on a context. The edge table admits what no reading of either field intends, and narrowing it needs the kinds each may legitimately reach to be decided rather than inferred.
